# The metric catalogue

Every number FlowCellar shows has one entry in the **metric catalogue**: its id, its label, how to read
it, and, for a check, its limits. The viewer takes its labels from it and the verdicts take their limits
and sentences from it. This page is written from catalogue version 0.1.1.

- Source: `catalogue/metrics_nanopore.yaml` in the repository.
- In the package: `flowcellar/catalogue/metrics_nanopore.json`. Read it with
  `python -c "from flowcellar import catalogue; print(catalogue.metric('fc_occupancy_first_hour'))"`.

## How a number becomes a verdict

A run gets one of **Pass**, **Warning**, **Fail**, **Incomplete** or **Running**, in two parts: **Run
health** (from MinKNOW's own files) and **Read data** (from the reads). Each part is the worst of its
checks, and a check has one of three roles:

| Role | What it can do |
|---|---|
| key | can set the run or sample verdict to fail |
| supporting | can set it to warn at most |
| shown only | shown, never changes the verdict |

A limit is one of these kinds:

- **fixed level**: "warning below 70 %". The levels in the tables below are the defaults; a library can
  change any of them (see the end of this page).
- **the run's own target**: the speed range the kit asks for, read from the run's files.
- **the lab's own history**: the run is placed against the earlier runs of the same kind in the same
  library (same device type, flow cell type and kit), as they were on the day the run started. History
  is used from 5 comparable runs, can warn but not fail until there are 8, and is not used for a
  verdict when the comparable runs differ widely from each other. A verdict is not changed by runs that
  come later.
- **a written-out rule**: for example "the run was ended by the instrument".

A check that cannot be assessed (no limit for this kind of run, the reads are not counted yet, the files
hold a different set of reads than the check is written for) says so with its reason; it never counts as
passed or failed.

## Run health

From the run folder alone; no basecalling is needed. The checks marked with * wait until the reads of the
run have been counted ("full detail").

| Check | Id | Role | Default limits | How to read |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| How the run ended | `run_stop_cause` | key | a written-out rule (see How to read) | Whether the run reached its planned end, was stopped by a person, or was ended by the instrument. |
| MinKNOW messages | `run_messages` | key | a written-out rule (see How to read) | Warnings and errors MinKNOW showed during the run, in its own words. Notices about the computer, such as disk space, are listed in the run log and do not count here. |
| Raw data written | `run_output_files` | supporting | a written-out rule (see How to read) | What MinKNOW wrote to disk, and whether every file reached its place. |
| * Speed through the pore | `dyn_speed_est_median` | key | the target range of the run's own kit, as MinKNOW recorded it | The typical speed of reads that ended normally, estimated from the signal. The kit sets a target range; well below it, quality and output drop. |
| Pores at the first scan | `fc_pores_first_scan` | key | PromethION: warning below 5,000<br>MinION / GridION: warning below 800<br>Flongle: warning below 50 | Pores that could sequence when the run began, counted with the library already on the flow cell. It is not the flow cell check done before loading, which is what ONT's warranty refers to. |
| Channels with a pore at the first scan | `fc_channels_with_pore_first_scan` | supporting | every run: warning below 65 % | One pore per channel sequences at a time, so this is how many channels could start at once. |
| Occupancy in the first hour | `fc_occupancy_first_hour` | key | every run: warning below 70 %, fail below 40 % | Occupancy is the share of working pores that were busy with a strand. It tells whether enough good library reached the pores. Measured from minute 30 to minute 90. |
| Occupancy over the run | `fc_occupancy_median` | supporting | every run: warning below 70 % | The middle value of occupancy across the whole run. |
| Blocked pores | `fc_recovering_frac` | key | every run: warning above 12 %, fail above 20 % | Pores that were blocked and being cleared, as a share of the time of pores that were still working. Dead channels are left out. |
| Blocked pores in the last third | `fc_recovering_last_third_frac` | supporting | every run: warning above 25 % | The same share late in the run: it shows blocking that builds up. |
| Temperature off target | `fc_temperature_max_dev_c` | supporting | every run: warning above 0.5 °C | The largest distance between the flow cell temperature and the target band during the run. |
| * Channels that produced reads | `fc_active_channels` | supporting | every run: warning below 65 % | Channels that gave any read at all during the run. |
| * Fall in speed over the run | `dyn_speed_drop_frac` | supporting | every run: warning above 15 % | Speed falls as the fuel in the buffer is used up. A large fall can be recovered by adding flush buffer. |
| * Reads that ended normally | `dyn_signal_positive_frac` | key | every run: warning below 90 %, fail below 80 % | A read ends normally when the strand leaves the pore by itself. The rest were ejected because a pore was blocked, or cut by a pore scan. |
| * Reads ejected from blocked pores | `dyn_unblock_frac` | supporting | every run: warning above 8 % | MinKNOW reverses the voltage to clear a blocked pore; the read in it ends there. |
| * Estimated read N50 | `len_est_n50` | supporting | genomic DNA: warning below 10,000 bases<br>cDNA: warning below 500 bases<br>direct RNA: warning below 800 bases | Read N50: half of all bases are in reads at least this long. Estimated from the signal before basecalling. |

### Output

The output of a run is judged at the last fixed time it reached (6 h, 12 h, 24 h, 48 h, 72 h), so that runs of different
length can be compared. The unit is reads for cDNA and direct RNA and estimated bases for genomic DNA,
unless the library's configuration sets `outcome_unit`. A run of under one hour is Incomplete. From one to
six hours the checks above apply but the output is not judged: the run is a Warning or a Fail when a check
says so, and Incomplete otherwise.

- With enough lab history the output is placed against it: a warning well below what is typical here,
  a fail far below it once the history rests on 8 comparable runs.
- Without history these fixed levels apply. They are stated for 72 h and scaled to the earlier times.

| Output | Id | Fixed levels at 72 h |
|---|---|---|
| Reads | `yield_reads_at_<hours>h` | PromethION, cDNA: warning below 50 M reads, fail below 25 M reads<br>PromethION, direct RNA: warning below 8 M reads, fail below 4 M reads<br>MinION / GridION, cDNA: warning below 5 M reads, fail below 2.5 M reads<br>MinION / GridION, direct RNA: warning below 800,000 reads, fail below 400,000 reads |
| Estimated bases | `yield_estimated_bases_at_<hours>h` | PromethION, cDNA: warning below 60 Gb, fail below 30 Gb<br>PromethION, genomic DNA: warning below 70 Gb, fail below 40 Gb<br>PromethION, direct RNA: warning below 15 Gb, fail below 8 Gb<br>MinION / GridION, genomic DNA: warning below 10 Gb, fail below 5 Gb<br>MinION / GridION, cDNA: warning below 6 Gb, fail below 3 Gb<br>MinION / GridION, direct RNA: warning below 1.5 Gb, fail below 700 Mb<br>Flongle: warning below 800 Mb, fail below 300 Mb |

Share of the 72 h level that applies at an earlier time:

| Assay | 6 h | 12 h | 24 h | 48 h | 72 h |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| cDNA | 12 % | 24 % | 45 % | 80 % | 100 % |
| direct RNA | 19 % | 35 % | 62 % | 92 % | 100 % |
| genomic DNA | 16 % | 30 % | 55 % | 85 % | 100 % |

On a flow cell that was loaded before, the run cannot be compared with fresh flow cells. Its output is
then judged as estimated bases per starting pore, against the lab's history of that number.

Other numbers are placed against the lab's history to explain a verdict (pores at the first scan,
occupancy over the first 24 h, pores left after 24 h, time spent sequencing, output per pore, output per
working channel-hour, speed, adapter share). They show as "differs from typical" and never change the
verdict of a run on a fresh flow cell.

## Read data

From the basecalled and aligned reads, when FlowCellar finds them. Every read is counted. A check is
assessed only on the set of reads it is written for: a share of passed reads, for instance, needs a file
that still holds the reads that failed. Checks on samples are assessed per sample; the worst sample
decides and the sentence names the samples.

| Check | Id | Role | Default limits | How to read |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Reads that passed the quality filter | `yield_pass_frac` | key | genomic DNA: warning below 90 %, fail below 75 %<br>cDNA: warning below 85 %, fail below 70 %<br>direct RNA: warning below 80 %, fail below 60 % | Share of reads (and bases) that passed the basecaller's quality filter. |
| Basecalled bases | `yield_basecalled_bases` | key | PromethION, cDNA: warning below 40 Gb, fail below 20 Gb<br>PromethION, genomic DNA: warning below 60 Gb, fail below 35 Gb<br>PromethION, direct RNA: warning below 12 Gb, fail below 6 Gb<br>MinION / GridION, genomic DNA: warning below 8 Gb, fail below 4 Gb<br>MinION / GridION, cDNA: warning below 4 Gb, fail below 2 Gb<br>MinION / GridION, direct RNA: warning below 1 Gb, fail below 500 Mb<br>Flongle: warning below 600 Mb, fail below 200 Mb | Bases that came out of the basecaller. |
| Read N50 | `len_n50` | key | genomic DNA: warning below 10,000 bases, fail below 3,000 bases<br>cDNA: warning below 700 bases, fail below 450 bases<br>direct RNA: warning below 900 bases, fail below 500 bases | Read N50 of the basecalled reads. |
| Median read length | `len_median` | supporting | cDNA: warning below 500 bases<br>direct RNA: warning below 600 bases | Typical basecalled read length. |
| Reads under 200 bases | `len_short_read_frac` | supporting | genomic DNA: warning above 10 %<br>cDNA: warning above 5 %<br>direct RNA: warning above 10 % | Share of reads shorter than 200 bases (adapter dimers, degraded input). |
| Median read quality | `qual_median` | key | R10, sup model: warning below Q 16, fail below Q 12<br>R10, hac model: warning below Q 13, fail below Q 10<br>R10, fast model: warning below Q 10, fail below Q 8<br>R9: warning below Q 12, fail below Q 9<br>RNA004, sup model: warning below Q 15, fail below Q 11<br>RNA004, hac model: warning below Q 12, fail below Q 9 | Typical read quality. |
| Mapped reads | `aln_mapped_frac` | key | genomic DNA: warning below 95 %, fail below 85 %<br>cDNA: warning below 92 %, fail below 80 %<br>direct RNA: warning below 90 %, fail below 75 % | Share of reads that aligned to the reference. |
| Median identity with the genome | `aln_identity_hist` | key | R10, sup model: warning below 97.5 %, fail below 96 %<br>R10, hac model: warning below 97 %, fail below 95 %<br>R9: warning below 94 %, fail below 90 %<br>RNA004: warning below 94 %, fail below 90 % | How closely reads match the reference: the practical accuracy of the run. |
| Reads split over several places in the genome | `aln_supplementary_frac` | supporting | genomic DNA: warning above 3 %<br>cDNA: warning above 3 %<br>direct RNA: warning above 2 % | Share of reads split over several places in the genome (chimeras, structural variants, fusions). |
| Full-length reads | `cdna_full_length_frac` | key | cDNA: warning below 80 %, fail below 60 % | Share of reads that are complete cDNA molecules with both primers, correctly oriented. |
| Reads that were two cDNAs joined together | `cdna_rescued_frac` | supporting | cDNA: warning above 2 % | Share of reads that were two or more cDNAs joined together and had to be cut apart. |
| Usable reads | `funnel_usable_frac` | key | genomic DNA: warning below 80 %, fail below 60 %<br>cDNA: warning below 55 %, fail below 35 %<br>direct RNA: warning below 60 %, fail below 40 % | Share of everything the flow cell sequenced that ended up as usable data. |
| Sequenced reads the basecaller did not keep | `funnel_basecall_loss_frac` | supporting | genomic DNA: warning above 15 %<br>cDNA: warning above 20 %<br>direct RNA: warning above 20 % | Share of sequenced reads the basecaller discarded (below the quality cut-off or unusable signal). |

## Changing a limit

The limits of the run health checks are changed per assay group (`gdna`, `cdna`, `drna`) in the library's
`flowcellar.toml`. The limits of the read data checks are the defaults above; this version has no setting
for them.

```toml
[profiles.cdna.rules.fc_occupancy_first_hour]
warn = 0.65            # a share is written as a fraction
# fail = 0.4           role = "supporting"           enabled = false
```

Then judge the runs again; no input is read: `flowcellar recompute --status-only --all -L DIR`.
See [Configuration](configuration.md).

## The numbers with a label

The catalogue describes 238 metrics and 70 numbers derived from them. It was written for the whole design, so it
also holds parts that this version does not compute: barcode balance, what is particular to direct RNA,
modified bases, adaptive sampling and duplex. The tables below list the numbers of the parts
that are built and that carry a label in the viewer. A number without a label is shown under a name made
from its id.

## Single-cell and spatial analyses

An analysis (an output folder of wf-single-cell or of Space Ranger) has a verdict of its own, made the same
way: the worst of its checks, key checks can fail it, supporting checks can warn. It never changes the
verdict of a flow cell run, and a flow cell run that is not in the library never lowers the verdict of an
analysis. A number whose source is missing is not available, never a failure, and a number
taken from a pipeline's report is marked "from report" on the page. The alarms a pipeline raises itself are
quoted word for word. This part is written from the add-on's catalogue, version 0.1.0
(`catalogue/metrics_singlecell_spatial.yaml`); its limits are first proposals, not tuned on any history.

| Check | Id | Role | From | Default limits | How to read |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pipeline alarms | `sp_pipeline_alarms` | key | Space Ranger | a written-out rule (see How to read) | Warnings and errors raised by Space Ranger itself, shown word for word. |
| Full-length rate | `sc_full_length_fraction` | key | wf-single-cell | warning below 80 %, fail below 60 % | Share of input reads that have the complete adapter pair. Low values point to a library-prep problem (fragmented cDNA, adapter dimers, chimeras). |
| Plus-strand share | `sc_strand_plus_fraction` | supporting | wf-single-cell | warning outside 35 % to 65 % | Share of stranded reads sequenced in the plus orientation. cDNA is read from either end at random, so this sits near one half; a value far from it means reads were lost on one side. |
| Valid barcode rate | `sc_valid_barcode_fraction` | key | wf-single-cell | warning below 70 %, fail below 50 % | Share of full-length reads that could be assigned to a cell, spot or square. For droplet data this is also the share of reads in called cells. |
| Valid UMI rate | `sc_valid_umi_fraction` | supporting | wf-single-cell | warning below 85 % | Share of barcoded reads that also have a usable UMI. |
| Gene assignment rate | `sc_gene_assigned_fraction` | key | wf-single-cell | warning below 55 %, fail below 40 % | Share of full-length reads that end up counted for a gene. This is the usable fraction of the library for gene expression. |
| Transcript assignment rate | `sc_transcript_assigned_fraction` | supporting | wf-single-cell | warning below 20 % | Share of full-length reads resolved to an isoform. |
| Mitochondrial read share | `sc_reads_chrm_fraction` | supporting | both pipelines | warning above 25 % | Share of aligned reads that map to the mitochondrial genome. High values mean stressed or dying cells, or free mitochondrial RNA. |
| Cells / spots / bins in the matrix | `sc_cells` | supporting | wf-single-cell | a written-out rule (see How to read) | Droplet data: cells called by the workflow. Visium: spots with data. Visium HD: 8 um bins with data. The label changes with the assay. |
| Mitochondrial fraction per cell / spot / bin | `sc_mito_fraction_per_barcode` | supporting | both pipelines | warning above 25 % | Share of each cell's UMIs that come from mitochondrial genes. High values mark damaged cells or necrotic tissue. |
| Spots / bins under tissue | `sp_units_under_tissue` | key | Space Ranger | a written-out rule (see How to read) | Capture units covered by tissue. Visium: spots. Visium HD: 2 um squares, 8 um bins and 16 um bins. |
| Reads under tissue | `sp_fraction_reads_under_tissue` | key | Space Ranger | warning below 50 %, fail below 30 % | Share of usable reads whose barcode lies under tissue. The rest landed on bare slide: RNA that leaked out of the tissue, or a tissue outline drawn too tight. |
| Cell segmentation summary | `sp_segmentation_summary` | supporting | Space Ranger | warning below 50 % | When Space Ranger segmented cells: how many, how much of the data they hold, and how big they are. |
| Image registration | `sp_registration` | supporting | Space Ranger | a written-out rule (see How to read) | How the tissue image was aligned to the capture area, and whether the automatic UMI-to-image check agreed. |
| Usable reads (Space Ranger) | `sr_usable_reads_fraction` | key | Space Ranger | warning below 30 %, fail below 10 % | Share of reads that survive every Space Ranger filter and are counted under tissue. One number for the efficiency of the whole experiment. |
| Valid barcodes (Space Ranger) | `sr_valid_barcodes` | key | Space Ranger | warning below 75 %, fail below 50 % | Share of reads whose barcode matches the slide's barcode list after correction. |
| Valid UMIs (Space Ranger) | `sr_valid_umis` | supporting | Space Ranger | warning below 75 % | Share of reads with a usable UMI. |
| Mapping breakdown (Space Ranger) | `sr_mapping` | supporting | Space Ranger | warning below 30 % | Where the reads map: genome, confidently, exonic, intronic, intergenic, transcriptome. |
| Reads antisense to genes (Space Ranger) | `sr_antisense_fraction` | key | Space Ranger | warning above 10 %, fail above 30 % | Share of reads on the wrong strand of a gene. High values mean the reads were not put into the orientation Space Ranger expects before conversion. |
| ONT workflow to Space Ranger UMI ratio | `sp_wf_sr_umi_ratio` | supporting | both pipelines | warning outside 0.5 to 2 | The same reads counted two ways: full-length long-read analysis against the short-read-style analysis. A large gap means one of the two pipelines is losing reads. |
| Workflow execution | `sc_wf_execution` | supporting | wf-single-cell | a written-out rule (see How to read) | Did the workflow finish cleanly, how long did it take and how much memory did it need. |
| Linked sequencing runs | `sc_link_runs` | shown only | both pipelines | a written-out rule (see How to read) | The flow cell runs this analysis was made from, with the share of reads from each and how the link was established. |

### The numbers of an analysis

| Label | Id | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| Input reads | `sc_input_reads` | reads |
| Full-length reads | `sc_full_length_reads` | reads |
| Adapter configuration | `sc_adapter_config_counts` | reads |
| Reads with a valid barcode | `sc_valid_barcode_reads` | reads |
| Reads assigned to a gene | `sc_gene_assigned_reads` | reads |
| Reads assigned to a transcript | `sc_transcript_assigned_reads` | reads |
| Read fate | `sc_read_funnel` | reads |
| Barcodes with reads | `sc_barcodes_detected` | count |
| Barcode rank plot | `sc_knee_curve` | reads |
| Cell-calling threshold | `sc_cell_threshold` | reads |
| Mean reads per cell / spot / bin | `sc_reads_per_cell_mean` | reads |
| Reads per barcode | `sc_reads_per_barcode` | reads |
| UMIs per cell / spot / bin | `sc_umis_per_barcode` | umis |
| Genes per cell / spot / bin | `sc_genes_per_barcode` | genes |
| Genes detected | `sc_total_genes_detected` | genes |
| Isoforms detected | `sc_total_transcripts_detected` | count |
| Unique molecules | `sc_unique_molecules` | umis |
| Sequencing saturation (ONT workflow) | `sc_saturation` | share |
| Reads per molecule | `sc_reads_per_molecule_hist` | count |
| Saturation curve | `sc_saturation_curve` | share |
| Mitochondrial UMI share | `sc_mito_umi_fraction` | share |
| Capture area under tissue | `sp_fraction_under_tissue` | share |
| UMIs under tissue | `sp_fraction_umis_under_tissue` | share |
| Mean reads per spot / bin under tissue | `sp_reads_per_unit_under_tissue` | reads |
| Genes per spot / bin under tissue | `sp_genes_per_unit` | genes |
| UMIs per spot / bin under tissue | `sp_umis_per_unit` | umis |
| Visium HD bin-level summary | `sp_bin_level_table` | table |
| UMIs and reads per mm2 of tissue | `sp_density_per_mm2` | per mm2 |
| Genes detected under tissue | `sp_total_genes_detected` | genes |
| Spatial QC map | `sp_map` | grid |
| Reads (Space Ranger) | `sr_number_of_reads` | reads |
| Sequencing saturation (Space Ranger) | `sr_sequencing_saturation` | share |
| Q30 bases (barcode, UMI, RNA read) | `sr_q30` | share |
| Library diagnostics (Space Ranger) | `sr_diagnostics` | share |
| Workflow parameters | `sc_wf_parameters` | table |
